They say we are going to have food shortages come this winter.

I have read much of the nations farm lands are under water from flooding.

Farmers were not able to plant crops this year in a lot of places.

Once our food reserves are gone, things could get tight.

Its best to prepare for the worst. Kinda why I started farming under the Obama admin. I didn't trust the SOB.

Prepping became a hobby, knowing I could feed my kids became a priority.

 

So this is what I got in the ground and everything looks good so far.

30 pepper plants (jalapeno, green, red, cayenne, thai)

16 tomato (cherry, beefsteak, roma)

12 cucumber

8 sunflowers

many different herbs (dill, oregano, mint, sage, rosemary to name a few)

15 green beans

10 Kale

10 lettuce

8 Zucchini

4 rows of potatoes

5 rows of corn

patch of onions

patch of garlic

row of carrots

row of beets

row of radish

Blueberries

strawberries

Asparagus

Brussel sprouts

Cabbage

Celery

2 apple tress

6 chickens (more eggs than I could ever eat)

I have it all being watered with a irrigation system on a timer.

In the fall I make the best salsa you ever tasted, also tomato sauce, spaghetti sauce, dill pickles, sweet pickles, pepper relish.

I make about 20 loaves of blueberry zucchini bread and freeze them.

The kale is washed, processed and stuffed in to gallon size freezer bags and frozen. Use this in my smoothies.

Potatoes can store throughout the winter in the basement.

Peppers are used for salsa, rest are frozen, cayenne are dehydrated used as a spice.

Corn cut off the cob, boiled and frozen and canned.

Strawberries washed and frozen. Used in smoothies.

Blue berries washed and frozen. Used in smoothies.

Carrots peeled, boiled and frozen and canned.

Radish processed and frozen. Used in smoothies.

Celery washed, chopped and dehydrated.

Brussel sprouts cut from the stalk, boiled and frozen.

Green bean cleaned and canned.

Herbs dehydrated

I stock up on noodles, flour, corn meal, powdered milk and rice. Buy 100 pounds of beef from the local butcher for the deep freezer.

Butter and cheese can be frozen.

I could hunker down for months and be just fine.

I think everyone should consider doing the same.

I'm sure the deep state has plans for us in the near future.

You never know what can happen, you always want to prep for the worst and hope for the best.

Other things to consider, first aid kit, generator, gasoline, wood burner, couple cords of woods, gun and ammo, batteries, water storage(bulk or bottles)

Our garden is just about done (FL). I have canned about 4 cases of squash and green beans out of it, but the 10-12 inches of rain we got last weekend pretty much finished it off. We will replant in august for an early fall garden. I have filled our freezers full of meat, so I will have to can our veggies. Last summer I canned several hundred pounds of meat too (beef, pork, and chicken).

I see bus loads of pickers on the roads right now, so our farmers are taking their crops to market. I will stop by the local produce store and pick up some peanuts, white acres, more green beans, tomatoes, etc to can.
